question: What is your age (in years)?
help_text: Subclass 500 applicants are usually 6+ for school sectors and 18+ for higher education. This is informational and rarely a problem for university applicants.
error_message: Enter your age in years. Subclass 500 typically requires applicants to be at least 6 for school sectors and 18 for higher education.

question: Are you applying from inside or outside Australia?
help_text: Most Pakistani applicants apply from outside Australia (offshore). This affects health-exam and biometric logistics, not eligibility.
error_message: Indicate whether you are applying from inside or outside Australia. This affects health exam and biometric logistics, not eligibility.

question: Are you the main (primary) student applicant?
help_text: The main applicant is the student. A spouse/children would be added as dependants with extra funds required.
error_message: Indicate whether you are the primary student applicant. A spouse or children added as dependants require additional funds evidence.

question: Do you already hold a valid Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) from your Australian institution?
help_text: You cannot lodge a Subclass 500 without a valid CoE from a CRICOS-registered provider. An offer letter is NOT a CoE — the CoE is issued after you accept and pay the deposit.
error_message: A valid Confirmation of Enrolment from a CRICOS-registered provider is mandatory. Your application cannot proceed without one — an offer letter is not a CoE.

question: Do you have your CoE number ready to enter in ImmiAccount?
help_text: The exact CoE number must be entered during lodgement. Keep the PDF from your provider handy.
error_message: The exact CoE number must be entered during lodgement in ImmiAccount. Keep the CoE PDF from your provider available.

question: If you have a packaged/multiple courses (e.g. foundation + degree), do you have a CoE for every course?
help_text: Packaged courses (common for pathway/foundation programs) need a CoE for each stage at lodgement.
error_message: For packaged or pathway programs, each course stage requires its own CoE at lodgement. A single CoE for only one stage is insufficient.

question: Is your institution CRICOS-registered? (Check at cricos.teqsa.gov.au)
help_text: Many Pakistani students are mis-sold by agents into non-CRICOS providers. Verify the provider yourself on the official CRICOS register before paying anything.
mapped_rule: Full-Time Enrolment at CRICOS-Registered Institution Required
error_message: Your institution must be registered on the CRICOS register. Verify the provider yourself at cricos.teqsa.gov.au before paying any agent or deposit.

question: Is your specific course (not just the institution) listed on CRICOS?
help_text: The exact course must be CRICOS-registered, not only the university. Search your course title on the CRICOS register.
mapped_rule: Full-Time Enrolment at CRICOS-Registered Institution Required
error_message: Your specific course — not just the institution — must be listed on the CRICOS register. Search the course title yourself at cricos.teqsa.gov.au.

question: Is your enrolment full-time?
help_text: Subclass 500 requires full-time study. Part-time enrolment is not eligible.
mapped_rule: Full-Time Enrolment at CRICOS-Registered Institution Required
error_message: Subclass 500 requires full-time enrolment. Part-time enrolment is not eligible and your application cannot proceed on that basis.

question: Have you prepared answers to the Genuine Student (GS) questions in the application form?
help_text: Since March 2024 the old GTE statement is replaced by GS questions answered directly in the form (ties at home, why this course/Australia, course-career benefit, plus any relevant facts). Weak/generic GS answers are the No.1 refusal reason for Pakistani applicants.
error_message: Since March 2024, the GS questions in the application form replace the old GTE statement. Weak or generic GS answers are the leading refusal cause for Pakistani applicants.

question: Can you give specific, documentable ties to Pakistan that show you will return (family, property, job offer, business, dependants)?
help_text: Vague ties ('my family is here') are weak. Strong ties are documentable: ancestral property in your name, a written return job offer, a family business you are part of, dependants relying on you.
error_message: Documentable ties to Pakistan — property in your name, a written return job offer, a family business, dependants relying on you — are stronger than vague claims about family.

question: Can you explain — in concrete terms — why this exact course and Australia, not just 'good universities'?
help_text: Officers reject generic reasons. Name the specific units, faculty, accreditation, or industry link that maps to YOUR background and a Pakistan-based career outcome.
error_message: Officers reject generic reasons for choosing Australia or this course. Name the specific units, faculty, accreditation, or industry link that connects to your background.

question: Can you explain how this qualification improves your career back in Pakistan (with a realistic salary/role)?
help_text: Show the path: current background → this course → a named role/sector in Pakistan. A course with no logical career payoff at home signals migration intent.
error_message: Show a clear path: your current background → this course → a named role or sector in Pakistan. A course with no logical career payoff at home signals migration intent.

question: Can you justify choosing Australia over cheaper/closer options (e.g. local universities, Malaysia, Gulf)?
help_text: EL3 officers probe 'why spend this much?'. Have a defensible reason tied to course quality/accreditation — not lifestyle or work rights.
error_message: Have a specific, defensible reason for choosing Australia over cheaper alternatives — one tied to course quality or accreditation, not lifestyle or work rights.

question: Does this course logically follow your previous education and/or work, or can you justify any switch?
help_text: A drastic, unexplained field change (e.g. MBBS → hospitality) is a classic refusal trigger. If you are switching, your GS answer must explain it credibly.
error_message: A drastic unexplained field change is a classic refusal trigger. If you are switching fields, your GS answer must connect your old and new fields with a credible career narrative.

question: Do you have documents (not just words) to back your intention to return to Pakistan?
help_text: Attach what you can: property papers, family business registration, a conditional return job letter. Documents beat narrative.
error_message: Documents supporting your return to Pakistan — property papers, business registration, a conditional return job letter — strengthen your GS case significantly.

question: Have you previously held an Australian student visa?
help_text: Informational. A prior compliant Australian visa can help; a prior breach must be disclosed in the immigration-history section.
error_message: Indicate whether you have previously held an Australian student visa. A prior compliant visa can support your case; a prior breach must be disclosed.

question: Do you have any education or employment gap longer than 12 months since Matric/FSc/A-Levels/Bachelors?
help_text: Gaps are common in Pakistan (exam delays, family reasons, work). A gap is not fatal by itself — an UNEXPLAINED gap is. This routes to the next question.
error_message: Education or employment gaps of over 12 months must be explained and evidenced. An unexplained gap is an Assessment Level 3 risk factor.

question: If you have a gap over 12 months, can you justify it with evidence (job letters, exam transcripts, family/medical reasons)?
help_text: Provide employment letters, salary slips, freelance/contract proof, or transcripts covering the gap years. 'I was preparing' without proof is weak.
error_message: An unexplained gap of over 12 months weakens your GS case at EL3. Provide employment letters, salary slips, freelance contracts, or transcripts covering the gap period.

question: Is your Australian course in a substantially different field from your last qualification?
help_text: A large field switch is allowed but heavily scrutinised at EL3. If yes, your GS answers must connect old and new fields with a credible career story.
error_message: A significant unexplained field switch is heavily scrutinised at Assessment Level 3. Your GS answers must connect your previous qualification to this course with a credible career narrative.

question: Are your academic transcripts/degrees verifiable and, where needed, attested (HEC/IBCC) and translated?
help_text: EL3 requires authenticated academic documents. Get HEC attestation for degrees and IBCC for FSc/Matric where applicable; provide certified English translations.
error_message: Assessment Level 3 requires authenticated academic documents. Obtain HEC attestation for degrees and IBCC attestation for Matric/FSc where applicable, with certified English translations.

question: What is your first-year tuition fee (in AUD) as shown on your CoE?
help_text: Enter the AUD figure from your CoE/offer. The tool adds living costs and airfare to compute your minimum required funds.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: Enter the first-year tuition in AUD as shown on your CoE. This figure is used to calculate the minimum funds required for your application.

question: How much money (in AUD equivalent) can you genuinely show as accessible for your studies?
help_text: Minimum = first-year tuition + AUD 29,710 living costs + ~AUD 2,500 airfare (plus extra for any dependants). Funds must be genuine and accessible, not just a number on paper.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: Funds must cover first-year tuition + AUD 29,710 living costs + ~AUD 2,500 return airfare. They must be genuine, accessible, and consistently held — not just a number on paper.

question: Do your funds cover first-year tuition + AUD 29,710 living costs + return airfare (and dependants if any)?
help_text: This is the core financial-capacity test. Under-funding is a top refusal cause. Use current figures — the living cost rose from 24,505 to 29,710 in 2024.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: Under-funding is a top refusal cause at Assessment Level 3. Your total evidence must cover tuition + AUD 29,710 living + return airfare, plus any dependant additions.

question: What is the MAIN source of your funds?
help_text: Each source has its own evidence trail. The follow-up questions check whether that trail is documented to EL3 standard.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: Each funding source requires its own paper trail. The follow-up questions check whether each source is documented to EL3 standard.

question: Have your funds been held in the account for at least 3 months (consistent balance), not just deposited recently?
help_text: EL3 expects a settled balance history (~3 months minimum). Unlike the UK there is no fixed 28-day rule, but a long consistent balance beats a recent lump sum every time.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: Assessment Level 3 expects approximately 3 months of consistent balance history. A balance that appears suddenly before applying signals arranged funds.

question: Do your (or your sponsor's) bank statements show a stable, consistent balance over several months?
help_text: Erratic statements (empty for months, then suddenly full) signal arranged funds and trigger verification calls to your bank.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: Erratic statements — empty for months then suddenly full — signal arranged funds and can trigger bank verification calls from the case officer.

question: Were there any large or sudden deposits in the last few months?
help_text: Large recent deposits are not banned — but each one must be explainable with a paper trail. This routes to the source-of-funds check.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: Large recent deposits are not barred but each must be explainable with a paper trail: a registered sale deed, salary record, loan letter, or notarised gift affidavit.

question: Can you document the source of every significant deposit (sale deed, salary, loan letter, gift affidavit)?
help_text: EL3's core test. Each major deposit needs proof: registered sale deed for property, FBR-declared salary, sanctioned loan letter, or a notarised gift affidavit from a traceable giver.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: Every significant deposit must have documentary proof: a registered sale deed, FBR-declared salary, formal bank loan letter, or a notarised gift affidavit from a traceable source.

question: If sponsored, is your sponsor an immediate family member (parent, spouse, sibling)?
help_text: Immediate-family sponsorship is expected and trusted. Distant relatives or 'family friends' as sponsors raise scrutiny and need a strong relationship + funds-source explanation.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: Distant-relative or 'family friend' sponsors attract greater scrutiny. An immediate family sponsor (parent, spouse, sibling) is expected and easier to establish.

question: If sponsored, does your sponsor file income tax returns with the FBR, matching the funds they are providing?
help_text: A sponsor showing large funds but no FBR tax history is a major red flag — it implies undeclared/untraceable income. Sponsor's declared income should plausibly support the amount.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: A sponsor with large funds but no FBR filing history implies undeclared income. The sponsor's declared income should plausibly match the amount they are providing.

question: If property sale is funding you, do you have the registered sale deed and bank-routed proceeds?
help_text: Property-sale funding is fine if the sale deed is registered and money entered the account through the banking channel — not cash.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: Property-sale proceeds are accepted if the sale deed is registered and the proceeds were routed through a banking channel — not received as cash.

question: If a loan is funding you, do you have an official sanction/disbursement letter from a recognised bank?
help_text: Education loans are accepted with a formal sanction letter from a recognised financial institution. Informal/family loans are not the same and carry less weight.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: An education loan requires a formal sanction letter from a recognised bank. Informal family loans carry less weight as financial evidence.

question: If including a partner/children, do you have the extra required funds for each dependant?
help_text: Add ~AUD 10,394 for a partner and ~AUD 4,449 per child to your required funds. Under-funding dependants invalidates the financial test.
mapped_rule: Financial Capacity — Must Cover Tuition, Living Costs, Travel
error_message: Each dependant requires additional funds (~AUD 10,394 for a partner, ~AUD 4,449 per child). Under-funding dependants invalidates the financial test.

question: Can you pay the Subclass 500 application charge (~AUD 2,000, separate from the funds you must show)?
help_text: The visa charge (~AUD 2,000 per primary applicant) is paid at lodgement and is separate from your evidence-of-funds. Confirm the current charge before lodging.
error_message: The Subclass 500 application charge (~AUD 2,000 per primary applicant) is paid at lodgement in ImmiAccount and is separate from your evidence-of-funds.

question: Have you arranged Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) from an Australian provider?
help_text: OSHC is mandatory and must be from an approved Australian provider. Pakistani/local health insurance is NOT accepted.
error_message: Overseas Student Health Cover from an approved Australian provider is mandatory. Local Pakistani or international insurance is not accepted.

question: Is your OSHC from an approved provider (Allianz, Bupa, Medibank, NIB, ahm)?
help_text: Only the five approved Australian OSHC providers count. Verify before paying.
error_message: Only OSHC from one of the five approved Australian providers (Allianz, Bupa, Medibank, NIB, ahm) is accepted. Verify the provider before purchasing.

question: Does your OSHC cover your full intended stay (and dependants), starting before course commencement?
help_text: Cover must span your whole visa period, starting ~1 week before classes. Gaps in OSHC breach visa conditions.
error_message: Your OSHC must cover your full visa period, starting approximately one week before courses commence. Any gap in cover breaches visa conditions.

question: Are you exempt from the English evidence requirement (e.g. prior study in English in an eligible country)?
help_text: Most Pakistani applicants are NOT exempt and must show IELTS/PTE/TOEFL. If unsure, assume you need a test.
error_message: Most Pakistani applicants are not exempt from the English evidence requirement. If you are unsure, assume a test is required.

question: If not exempt, do you have a valid approved English test result (IELTS/PTE/TOEFL/Cambridge)?
help_text: A valid result is required unless genuinely exempt. Minimum IELTS 5.5 overall for the visa; your course often needs higher (6.0–7.0).
error_message: A valid approved English test result (IELTS, PTE, TOEFL iBT, or Cambridge) is required unless you are genuinely exempt. The visa minimum is IELTS 5.5 overall.

question: Does your English score meet BOTH your course requirement and the visa minimum?
help_text: Meeting the visa floor (IELTS 5.5) is not enough if your university needs 6.5. Both must be satisfied.
error_message: Your English score must satisfy both the visa minimum (IELTS 5.5) and your course's own requirement. Meeting only the visa floor is not sufficient if the course needs more.

question: Have you generated your HAP ID in ImmiAccount to book your health exam?
help_text: The HAP ID lets you book the medical. Generate it early — panel-clinic slots in Pakistan can be limited.
error_message: Generate your HAP ID in ImmiAccount early to book your health examination. Panel-clinic appointment slots in Pakistan can fill up quickly.

question: Have you completed (or booked) the required health examination?
help_text: A health exam is mandatory. Pakistani applicants almost always need a chest X-ray for TB screening.
error_message: A health examination at an approved panel physician is mandatory. Pakistani applicants almost always require a chest X-ray for TB screening.

question: Will you use an approved panel physician / Bupa Medical Visa Services (not a random local clinic)?
help_text: Only exams at approved panel clinics count. A cheaper local clinic's report is worthless for the visa and wastes money.
error_message: Only health examinations conducted by IRCC-approved panel physicians are accepted. A report from a local clinic not on the panel list is worthless for the visa.

question: Have you lived in any country other than Pakistan for 12+ months in the last 10 years?
help_text: If yes, you need a police clearance from that country too. Routes to the next question.
error_message: If you have lived in any country other than Pakistan for 12 or more months in the last 10 years, you will need a police clearance from that country as well.

question: Do you have (or can obtain) police clearances for every country where you lived 12+ months?
help_text: Pakistani applicants typically need a PCC from NADRA/local police; add clearances for any other country of long residence.
error_message: Pakistani applicants typically need a PCC from NADRA or local police. If you have lived abroad for 12+ months, you also need clearances from those countries.

question: Will you disclose any criminal/character matters fully and accurately?
help_text: Hiding a character issue is an independent refusal ground — worse than the issue itself. Disclose everything.
error_message: Hiding a character issue is an independent refusal ground — often more damaging than the underlying matter itself. Disclose everything accurately.

question: Have you EVER had a visa refusal, cancellation, or overstay in any country (UK, Canada, USA, Schengen, etc.)?
help_text: Prior refusals (especially UK/Canada/USA) are visible to Australia and heavily scrutinised. A refusal is survivable IF disclosed and explained — concealment is fatal.
error_message: Prior refusals or breaches in any country are visible to Australian case officers and will be heavily scrutinised. Concealment is an independent refusal ground.

question: If yes, which country/countries and what was the stated reason?
help_text: Note each refusal and its reason. You will need to address each one in your application and GS answers.
error_message: Record each prior refusal, its country, and the stated reason. You will need to address each one in your GS answers and supporting documents.

question: Will you disclose ALL prior refusals/breaches in this application (nothing omitted)?
help_text: Non-disclosure of immigration history is an independent refusal ground and can trigger a re-entry ban (PIC 4020). Disclose everything, even old/minor matters.
error_message: Non-disclosure of immigration history is an independent refusal ground and can trigger a PIC 4020 three-year exclusion. Disclose everything, including old or minor matters.

question: Have you ever claimed asylum or protection in any country?
help_text: An asylum claim history strongly conflicts with 'temporary student returning home' and must be addressed candidly with legal advice if it applies.
error_message: A prior asylum claim strongly conflicts with temporary student intent and must be disclosed and addressed candidly, ideally with qualified legal advice.

question: Are you switching to a course at a lower level than a visa you already hold?
help_text: Relevant only if you already hold a student visa and want to drop to a lower AQF level. Routes to the AQF check.
mapped_rule: Course Must Be at the Same or Higher AQF Level (Condition 8202)
error_message: Indicate whether you are switching to a different course level. Dropping to a lower AQF level on the same visa breaches Condition 8202.

question: If changing courses, is the new course at the SAME or HIGHER AQF level?
help_text: Dropping to a lower AQF level on the same visa breaches Condition 8202 and risks cancellation. You'd need a new Subclass 500.
mapped_rule: Course Must Be at the Same or Higher AQF Level (Condition 8202)
error_message: Dropping to a lower AQF level on the same visa breaches Condition 8202 and risks visa cancellation. You would need to apply for a new Subclass 500.

question: Do you understand the 48-hours-per-fortnight work limit during study?
help_text: Work is capped at 48 hours/fortnight while classes are in session (unlimited during scheduled breaks). Breaching it risks cancellation.
mapped_rule: Work Limited to 48 Hours Per Fortnight During Study
error_message: Work is capped at 48 hours per fortnight while classes are in session (unlimited during scheduled breaks). Exceeding this limit breaches your visa conditions.

question: Do you understand you must stay enrolled full-time and meet satisfactory academic progress?
help_text: Condition 8202: maintain full-time enrolment and progress. Failing this is a common cause of cancellation for students who treat study as secondary.
mapped_rule: Must Maintain Full-Time Enrolment and Satisfactory Academic Progress
error_message: Under Condition 8202, you must maintain full-time enrolment and satisfactory academic progress. Failing these requirements can lead to visa cancellation.

question: Did an education agent/consultant prepare or submit any of your documents?
help_text: Using an agent is fine — but YOU are legally responsible for everything submitted under your name. Routes to the verification check.
error_message: Using an education agent is permitted, but you are legally responsible for everything submitted in your name, regardless of who prepared it.

question: Have you personally read and verified EVERY document and form answer submitted in your name?
help_text: Unscrupulous agents inflate bank balances, fake experience letters, or alter transcripts. If an agent fabricated anything, YOU face refusal and a PIC 4020 ban. Verify every line yourself.
error_message: You must personally verify every document and answer submitted in your name. Agent-fabricated content — false balances, altered transcripts — makes you liable for refusal and a PIC 4020 ban.

question: Is your agent registered/reputable (e.g. linked to the institution, MARA agent), rather than an unknown local middleman?
help_text: Prefer agents authorised by your institution or a registered migration agent. 'Guaranteed visa' middlemen are the source of most fraud-related refusals.
error_message: Use an agent authorised by your institution or a registered migration agent (MARA). Unregistered 'guaranteed visa' middlemen are the primary source of fraud-related refusals.
